questions.question: What does VideoPatch3D turn a video into before transformer blocks?
options: One class label per complete video
A list of text captions with no pixel features
Spatiotemporal tokens from strided 3D convolution blocks
questions.explanation: The patchifier groups neighboring time, height, and width positions so the transformer can process a token sequence.

questions.question: For input (1,4,8,16,16) and patch sizes (2,2,2), how many tokens are produced?
questions.explanation: The code treats the shape as (batch, channels, time, height, width): the token grid is (8/2,16/2,16/2)=(4,8,8), so it contains 4*8*8=256 tokens; channels do not add token positions.

questions.question: How is divided attention organized in the video transformer?
options: Only the first video frame receives attention
Temporal attention runs within each spatial location, then spatial attention runs across locations
Spatial attention is replaced by an image classifier
The model attends to text but never to neighboring frames
questions.explanation: Factorizing the operation separates time and space, reducing the cost of a full attention matrix over all video tokens.

questions.question: What output shape does the TinyVideoDiT example report for its token features?
questions.explanation: After patchifying the example video, the transformer keeps a batch of 256 tokens with embedding width 32.

questions.question: What makes a video world model action-conditioned?
options: It predicts only the next action from a single still image
It removes time so all frames share one state
It uses a larger RGB palette without an action input
Its prediction of future frames also receives the actions taken by the agent
questions.explanation: Conditioning on actions lets the model simulate how different decisions can change the future observation sequence.
